In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that the use of DOAC in the first 24 hours of stroke is safe or effective.
the initiation of DOACs within two weeks from NVAF-related AIS onset in patients who undergo urgent reperfusion with systemic thrombolysis/ mechanical thrombectomy is safe and efficacious.
DOACs can be started within 14 days of stroke onset in patients with NVAF and ischemic stroke who are undergoing urgent reperfusions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of DOACs is safe and effective in patients with NVAF-related AIS.
urgent reperfusion of NVAF-related stroke is feasible, safe, and efficacious.
DOACs can be started early in NVAF patients who have had an AIS and are undergoing urgent reperfection, but the safety and efficacy of these agents has not been established in this setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DOACs seems to be safe in the early phase (within two weeks from stroke onset) in patients with NVAF undergoing urgent reperfusions for AIS.
DOACs may be started in the early phase after AIS onset in NVAF patients undergoing urgent revascularization.
DOACs can be safely introduced in the early phase after AIS onset in patients with NVAF undergoing urgent reperfusions.
